notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs during-work/before-course for data-tier rules, research facts and course-design items; resolved by treating principles and facts as general and rules on what a user does with a tool as during-work. (2) modality, mostly informs vs must-not/may for consequence statements and permissions; resolved by using must-not for 'is a violation'/'cannot' prohibitions, informs for 'will be treated as' consequences, may for permissions. (3) policy_type, mainly P02 vs P05/P35 for the three syllabus templates (tier text coded P02 with may; integrating AI into assignments coded P35), P26 vs P25 for the tool/how/why appendix (P25), P24 vs P25 for citation style (P25), P59 vs P17 for the Anthology AI Design Assistant (P59), and UNCOVERED vs P53 for instructor ethics discussion (P53). The phishing/deepfake security caution stays UNCOVERED. (4) actor, student vs all for the output-restriction clause (student). Single-coder units were checked against the text: most were real distinct sentences and were kept; 3 dropped (Writing Center referral, a bare pointer to the acceptable use policy, and an acknowledgement of AI feedback potential). One cross-anchored pair (AI Design Assistant passage) was merged by hand and counted as matched. Document stance: delegates for all three documents.
